--address.help: The <address> that the new CA will listen at.

--admin-cert.help: Admin certificate (<chain>) in PEM format to store in the 'x5c' header of a JWT.

--admin-provisioner,admin-issuer.help: The provisioner <name> to use for generating admin credentials.

--admin-subject,admin-name.help: The admin <subject> to use for generating admin credentials.

--all.help: uninstall from Firefox's, Java's, and the system's default trust store

--api-url.help: URL where the Smallstep API can be found

--attestation-ca-insecure.help: Disables TLS server validation when connecting to the Attestation CA

--attestation-ca-root.help: The path to the PEM <file> with trusted roots when connecting to the Attestation CA

--attestation-ca-url.help: The base url of the Attestation CA to use

--audience.help: Request a token for an audience other than the API Gateway

--base.help: Return the base of the step path

--browser.help: Path to browser for OAuth flow (macOS only).

--ca-kms.help: The <uri> to configure the KMS used for signing the certificate

--ca-url.help: <URI> of the targeted Step Certificate Authority.

--comment.help: The comment used when adding the certificate to an agent. Defaults to the subject if not provided.

--config.help: path to the config file to use for CLI flags

--crl-endpoint.help: The CRL endpoint to use. If not provided step will attempt to check it against the certificate's CRLDistributionPoints extension endpoints.

--dictionary,dict.help: The <file> to use as a dictionary to get random words.

--dry-run.help: Executes the command without changing any file.

--exec.help: The <command> to run after the certificate has been rekeyed.

--f,force.help: Force the overwrite of files without asking.

--fingerprint.help: The <fingerprint> of the targeted root certificate.

--firefox.help: uninstall from the Firefox NSS security database

--implicit.help: Uses the implicit flow to authenticate the user. Requires **--insecure** and **--client-id** flags.

--install.help: Install the root certificate into the system's default trust store.

--java.help: uninstall from the Java key store

--jwt.help: Generate a JWT Auth token instead of an OAuth Token (only works with service accounts)

--key.help: The path of an existing key <file> of the root certificate authority.

--legacy.help: Encodes PKCS#12 files using the algorithms that were traditionally used, PBE+SHA1+RC2 for certificates and PBE+SHA1+3DES for keys.

--listen-url.help: The redirect_uri <url> in the authorize request (e.g. "http://127.0.0.1:10000")

--min-password-length.help: Set minimum required length for password used to encrypt private key. The default value is '0'. Values <=0 are interpreted as if no minimum value is set.

--nebula-cert.help: Certificate <file> in PEM format to store in the 'nebula' header of a JWT.

--no-agent.help: Do not add the generated certificate and associated private key to the SSH agent.

--no-system.help: disables the uninstall from the system's default trust store

--oidc.help: Output OIDC Token instead of OAuth Access Token

--out,output-file.help: The new certificate <file> path. Defaults to overwriting the <crt-file> positional argument

--output-file.help: The destination <file> of the generated one-time token.

--pkcs8.help: Convert RSA and ECDSA private keys to PKCS#8 PEM/DER format.

--pki.help: Generate only the PKI without the CA configuration.

--pkix.help: Use the PKIX marshaling format instead of X.509.

--raw.help: Print the raw bytes instead of the fingerprint. These bytes can be piped to a different hash command.

--redirect-url.help: The <url> to open in the system browser when the OAuth flow is successful.

--root.help: The path of an existing PEM <file> to be used as the root certificate authority.

--set-file.help: The JSON <file> with the template data variables.

--short.help: Print the certificate or CSR details in shorter and more friendly format.

--skip-csr-signature.help: Skip creating and signing a CSR.

--sshpop-cert.help: Certificate (<chain>) in PEM format to store in the 'sshpop' header of a JWT.

--team.help: The team <ID> used to bootstrap the environment.

--tpm-storage-directory.help: The directory where TPM keys and certificates will be stored

--u,url.help: use the encoding format typically used in URLs and file names

--verify-crl.help: Verify the certificate against it's CRL.

--verify-ocsp.help: Verify the certificate against it's OCSP.

--x5c-cert.help: Certificate (<chain>) in PEM format to store in the 'x5c' header of a JWT.

--x5c-insecure.help: Use the JWT header 'x5cInsecure' instead of 'x5c'.

--x5t-cert.help: Certificate <file> in PEM format to use for the 'x5t' header of a JWS or JWT
